correctness.rationale: For four adjacent characters, support sizes 1,2,3,4 yield respectively 12,54,108,81 nonzero character terms. Weil bounds plus exact root exclusions give 256 N >= p-513 sqrt(p)-256. The integer square test at 263681 is positive and monotone thereafter. C++17 exact enumeration checks each of 11,538 eligible primes below 263681; 144 fail full coverage, last at 3361, whose sole missing code is 195. A mathematically independent direct coset implementation verifies every eligible prime through 4000, including all 144 failures. The code is compiled/replayed from actual new package paths; no inference from finite data to an infinite tail is made.

value.rationale: The complete 4^4 quartic-character word language is a canonical next-order finite-word invariant; sharp first universal prime 3373 and 144 fully classified exceptions cannot be inferred from asymptotic existence alone. A new mixed terminal obstruction persists at 3361 even though an all-residue quadruple is present, unlike the previously known three-letter terminal all-zero failure. This structural separation and exact cutoff motivate the invariant beyond a routine numerical increment; the work does not claim the underlying character sum as new.
